{{Short description|British theoretical physicist, FRS (1952–2021)}}

'''Mark Warner''' FRS<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Terentjev |first1=Eugene |last2=Jardine-Wright |first2=Lisa |date=2024 |title=Mark Warner. 26 January 1952—24 December 2021 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2024.0016 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=77|pages=417–434 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2024.0016 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (26 January 1952 – 24 December 2021) was a New Zealand-British physicist. He was a pioneer in the field of [[liquid crystal]] elastomers,<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Warner |first1=Mark |title=Liquid Crystal Elastomers |last2=Michael Terentjev |first2=Eugene |date=2006 |publisher=Oxford University Press |isbn=9780198527671}}</ref> and proponent of physics education in the UK.

== Life ==
Born and raised in New Zealand, Mark Warner arrived in the UK after being awarded a scholarship in 1969 to study at [[Corpus Christi College, Cambridge]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021 |title=Professor Mark Warner FRS (26 January 1952 - 24 December 2021) |url=https://www.corpus.cam.ac.uk/articles/professor-mark-warner-frs-26-january-1952-24-december-2021}}</ref> where he would be based for the majority of his career.

After completing his PhD on the molecular motion of polymeric systems, he moved to [[Stanford University|Stanford]] for a postdoctoral position that introduced him to liquid crystals, the field that would define his research career. Recognition of his work in liquid crystal elastomers included the 2003 EuroPhysics Prize from the [[European Physical Society]].<ref name= Obituary>{{Cite web |date=23 January 2022|title=Mark Warner obituary |url=https://www.theguardian.com/science/2022/jan/23/mark-warner-obituary |publisher= [[The Guardian]]}}</ref>

Beyond research, Mark also played an important role in physics education in schools, culminating in the Isaac Physics program, which he founded with [[Lisa Jardine-Wright|Prof. Lisa Jardine-Wright]]. They were awarded [[Institute of Physics|IOP]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021 |title=Professor Mark Warner FRS FInstP (1952-2021) |url=https://www.iop.org/physics-community/obituaries/professor-mark-warner}}</ref> Lawrence Bragg Medal and Prize for this initiative.

He was made an Honorary Fellow of the [[Royal Society Te Apārangi|Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 2002, and Fellow of [[Royal Society|the Royal Society]] in 2012.<ref name= Obituary />
